title: MC68000 exception vectors
covers: The MC68000's exception vectors: reset, bus and address error, the instruction traps, trace, the line A and line F emulators, the autovectors and the TRAP vectors

rows.text: Vector 0, at address 0x000, is Reset: Initial SSP, in supervisor program space.
Vector 1, at address 0x004, is Reset: Initial PC, in supervisor program space.
The reset vector requires four words, unlike the other vectors, and is located in the supervisor program space.
The processor is forced into the supervisor state, and the trace state is forced off.
The interrupt priority mask is set at level 7.
The vector number is internally generated to reference the reset exception vector at location 0.
The address in the first two words of the reset exception vector is fetched as the initial SSP.
The address in the last two words of the reset exception vector is fetched as the initial program counter.
Instruction execution is started at the address in the program counter.
The initial program counter should point to the power-up/restart code.
The first vector read step stores the previous m_dbin into the high half of m_da[16], the SSP slot; the next step stores the word read into it.
device_reset starts the core in the S_RESET state, the first of the special states, which the generator lists as reset.
The register m_pc is stored from m_au, which holds the address fetched from the vector plus 2.
Table 6-2's row for vector 2 reads 2 2 8 008 SD Bus Error.
The status register is copied, the supervisor mode is entered, and tracing is turned off.
The vector number is generated to refer to the bus error vector.
Additional information is saved on the supervisor stack; the program counter and the copy of the status register are saved.
The processor saves its internal copy of the first word of the instruction being processed.
The processor saves the address being accessed by the aborted bus cycle.
Specific information about the access is also saved: type of access (read or write), processor activity and function code outputs.
The processor commences instruction processing at the address in the vector.
The generator lists a bus_error state whose code passes vector number 2 to the exception hook and sets a vector offset of 0x0008.
Table 6-2's row for vector 3 reads 3 3 12 00C SD Address Error.
An address error exception occurs when the processor attempts to access a word or long-word operand at an odd address.
An address error exception occurs when the processor attempts to access an instruction at an odd address.
The vector number refers to the address error vector.
The exception processing sequence is the same as that for a bus error, including the information to be stacked.
The supervisor stack order for a bus or address error exception includes the status register and the program counter.
The supervisor stack order for a bus or address error exception includes the instruction register.
The supervisor stack order for a bus or address error exception includes the access address.
The supervisor stack order for a bus or address error exception includes the R/W bit, the function code and the I/N bit.
The generator lists an address_error state whose code passes vector number 3 to the exception hook and sets a vector offset of 0x000C.
Table 6-2's row for vector 4 reads 4 4 16 010 SD Illegal Instruction.
An instruction word that matches no legal instruction pattern, once fetched, causes an illegal instruction exception.
The bit pattern $4AFC, the ILLEGAL instruction, forces an illegal instruction exception.
The exception stack frame for group 2 is pushed on the supervisor stack.
The illegal instruction vector is fetched.
The generator lists an illegal state whose code passes vector number 4 to the exception hook and sets a vector offset of 0x0010; decoding starts every opcode as S_ILLEGAL.
Table 6-2's row for vector 5 reads 5 5 20 014 SD Zero Divide.
An unsigned divide (DIVU) instruction forces an exception if a division operation is attempted with a divisor of zero.
A signed divide (DIVS) instruction forces an exception if a division operation is attempted with a divisor of zero.
Eleven divu.w forms are listed, differing in the first operand; divu_w_ds_dd_df, for a data register source, takes the trap sequence with vector number 5 and vector offset 0x0014.
Eleven divs.w forms are listed, differing in the first operand; divs_w_ds_dd_df, for a data register source, takes the trap sequence with vector number 5 and vector offset 0x0014.
Table 6-2's row for vector 6 reads 6 6 24 018 SD CHK Instruction.
The chk_w_ds_dd_df handler (list: chk.w ds dd) takes the trap sequence with vector number 6 and vector offset 0x0018.
Table 6-2's row for vector 7 reads 7 7 28 01C SD TRAPV Instruction.
TRAPV: if the V flag is set, then TRAP.
The TRAPV instruction forces an exception if the user program detects a run-time error, which may be an arithmetic overflow.
The trapv_df handler (list: trapv) takes the trap sequence with vector number 7 and vector offset 0x001C.
Table 6-2's row for vector 8 reads 8 8 32 020 SD Privilege Violation.
An attempt to execute AND immediate to SR, EOR immediate to SR or OR immediate to SR while in the user mode causes an exception.
An attempt to execute MOVE USP, RESET, RTE or STOP while in the user mode causes an exception.
MOVE to SR is listed among the privileged instructions as 68010 only.
The status register is copied; the supervisor mode is entered; and tracing is turned off.
The vector number is generated to reference the privilege violation vector.
The current program counter and the copy of the status register are saved on the supervisor stack.
Instruction execution commences at the address in the privilege violation exception vector.
The move_ds_sr_df handler, listed as move with operands ds and sr, tests the supervisor bit and raises the privilege exception in user mode.
The generator lists a state spelled priviledge whose code passes vector number 8 to the exception hook and sets a vector offset of 0x0020.
Table 6-2's row for vector 9 reads 9 9 36 024 SD Trace.
If the T bit is set at the beginning of the execution of an instruction, a trace exception is generated after the instruction is completed.
A copy is made of the status register; the transition to supervisor mode is made, and the T bit is turned off.
The vector number is generated to reference the trace exception vector.
The current program counter and the copy of the status register are saved on the supervisor stack.
Instruction execution commences at the address contained in the trace exception vector.
The generator lists a trace state whose code passes vector number 9 to the exception hook and sets a vector offset of 0x0024.
Table 6-2's row for vector 10 reads A 10 40 028 SD Line 1010 Emulator.
Word patterns with bits 15-12 equaling 1010 or 1111 are distinguished as unimplemented instructions, and separate exception vectors are assigned to them.
The generator lists a linea state whose code passes vector number 10 to the exception hook and sets a vector offset of 0x0028.
Table 6-2's row for vector 11 reads B 11 44 02C SD Line 1111 Emulator.
Opcodes beginning with 1111 are coprocessor instructions in the MC68020 and beyond; the separate vectors allow the operating system to emulate unimplemented instructions in software.
The generator lists a linef state whose code passes vector number 11 to the exception hook and sets a vector offset of 0x002C.
The generator adds the packed decode table entry { 0xf000, 0xf000, S_LINEF }, and init_decode_table stores S_LINEF for each opcode it matches whose slot still holds S_ILLEGAL.
Table 6-2's row for vector 25 reads 19 25 100 064 SD Level 1 Interrupt Autovector.
If external logic requests an automatic vector, the processor internally generates a vector number corresponding to the interrupt level number.
When the cpu space id is AS_CPU_SPACE with no configured map, default_autovectors_map maps address mask + 0x3 to a read returning autovector(1), which is 0x18 plus the level.
Table 6-2's row for vector 26 reads 1A 26 104 068 SD Level 2 Interrupt Autovector.
When the cpu space id is AS_CPU_SPACE with no configured map, default_autovectors_map maps address mask + 0x5 to a read returning autovector(2), which is 0x18 plus the level.
Table 6-2's row for vector 27 reads 1B 27 108 06C SD Level 3 Interrupt Autovector.
When the cpu space id is AS_CPU_SPACE with no configured map, default_autovectors_map maps address mask + 0x7 to a read returning autovector(3), which is 0x18 plus the level.
Table 6-2's row for vector 28 reads 1C 28 112 070 SD Level 4 Interrupt Autovector.
When the cpu space id is AS_CPU_SPACE with no configured map, default_autovectors_map maps address mask + 0x9 to a read returning autovector(4), which is 0x18 plus the level.
Table 6-2's row for vector 29 reads 1D 29 116 074 SD Level 5 Interrupt Autovector.
When the cpu space id is AS_CPU_SPACE with no configured map, default_autovectors_map maps address mask + 0xb to a read returning autovector(5), which is 0x18 plus the level.
Table 6-2's row for vector 30 reads 1E 30 120 078 SD Level 6 Interrupt Autovector.
When the cpu space id is AS_CPU_SPACE with no configured map, default_autovectors_map maps address mask + 0xd to a read returning autovector(6), which is 0x18 plus the level.
Table 6-2's row for vector 31 reads 1F 31 124 07C SD Level 7 Interrupt Autovector.
When the cpu space id is AS_CPU_SPACE with no configured map, default_autovectors_map maps address mask + 0xf to a read returning autovector(7), which is 0x18 plus the level.
Table 6-2's row for vectors 32 to 47 reads 20-2F 32-47 128 080 SD TRAP Instruction Vectors.
TRAP #n uses vector number 32+n.
The status register is copied; the supervisor mode is entered; and tracing is turned off.
The vector number is internally generated; for the TRAP instruction, part of the vector number comes from the instruction itself.
The program counter and the copy of the status register are saved on the supervisor stack.
Instruction execution commences at the address in the exception vector.
The TRAP instruction forces an exception.
The handler trap_imm4 is listed under opcode pattern 4e40 with mask fff0, which spans sixteen instruction words, and takes its vector offset from their low four bits.

searched.gave: the core's sources cite no manual
the user's manual lists TRAP vectors 32 to 47 as one table row, which entry m68000:vector:32 holds

rows.text: trap_imm4 (pattern 4e40, mask fff0) stores 0x80 | ((ird & 0xf) << 2) in m_ftu as the vector offset; for low four bits 1 that is 0x84.
The decode table has an entry for pattern 0x4e40 under mask 0xfff0, the pattern and mask in the header comment of trap_imm4, so 0x4E41 matches it.
